subject.title: Config: scaffold compaction loop guard settings

question: Should OpenClaw accept a reserved `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` namespace now, or should saturated-session guard policy build on the existing `tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard` and compaction quality-guard surfaces first?
rationale: The patch is mechanically focused, but new config/default surfaces are compatibility-sensitive and current main already has an adjacent shipped guard under a different namespace.

options.title: Defer To Canonical Design
options.body: Keep this PR open but paused while maintainers settle the namespace, defaults, and runtime semantics in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48238.

options.title: Adopt This Namespace
options.body: Proceed with `agents.defaults.compaction.guard` only after adding real proof, refreshing the branch, and documenting how it coexists with or supersedes the existing guard path.

options.title: Close And Redesign
options.body: Close this branch if maintainers decide the separate compaction guard namespace should not become public config.

recommendation.title: Defer To Canonical Design
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but paused while maintainers settle the namespace, defaults, and runtime semantics in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48238.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the adjacent post-compaction guard, scoped config behavior, and merge ownership for this area.
